correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the mechanism and all quantifiers from the frozen RESULT: A1,A2 partition the half-line, giving φ1(x)+φ2(x)=2√π√x, while 0<φ2(x)↑L<2. Positive-initial cooperative ODE solutions have monotone zero-argument limit u, and differentiation of √(u1+u2) yields √π≤∂t√(u1+u2)≤√(2π), proving πt²≤sum≤2πt² and nonzero u for t>0. Since u2≤2Lt, u1→∞ and then u2→∞, yielding u2/t→2L. With r=√u1, the exact equation gives r=√π t+2√(2L)√t+o(√t), hence u1=πt²+4√(2πL)t^{3/2}+o(t^{3/2}). The zero-start Laplace cumulant identity implies Pz(ζ>t)=exp(−z·u(t)), almost sure finite-time explosion for all finite z≥0 nonzero and the distinct type-specific exponents. Independently evaluated stable integral partitions and numerical ODE trajectories as finite illustrations, not infinite proof.
residual_risks: The zero-argument limit identifies cemetery explosion, not extinction at zero; the latter is not claimed.
ODE numerical samples to t=200 and finite Lévy truncations do not certify large-time asymptotics.
The growth expansion is for this one fixed mechanism and does not assume arbitrary modifications of A1/A2.

value.rationale: The starting paper expressly identifies this concrete multitype conservativity mechanism as undecided. The exact nonconservativity verdict plus genuinely different type-one quadratic and type-two linear log-survival scales, and computable t^{3/2} correction, is an independently meaningful branching-process finding rather than an elementary renaming of a criterion. It gives an explicit boundary example for the reach of componentwise Grey tests.
residual_risks: These are explosion-time survival asymptotics for the fixed interleaved partition, not a universal multitype Grey theorem.

limitations: Explosion (cemetery) not extinction at zero; fixed interleaved mechanism only; no sample-path explosion rate inference.
